text:
marta: Quick proposal — change the x-redwood-variant header shape so it carries a tiny opt-in token and a short route id. Goal: allow SDKs to explicitly opt users into client-side A/B routing without server-side flags. PTAL before EOD; want to lock API for next SDK push.

jasper: +1 on opt-in header, want the format spelled out. prefer a compact delimiter-based header rather than embedding JSON.

marta: agreed. draft format below:

```http
# example header values
x-redwood-variant: canary-v2;opt_in=1;rid=42
x-redwood-trace: 7d3a2f9c
```

li: Question: what does rid map to? deterministic bucketing key? we should avoid server-side state when possible. Also proxies sometimes fold headers — small and simple is good.

marta: rid is an opaque 1-3 byte integer that maps to a client-side routing shard. Server routing policy will interpret rid when opt_in=1, otherwise ignore. The SDK will generate rid via consistent hash of user id + salt.

ben: Mobile SDKs historically have trouble sending custom headers for background requests and some webviews strip headers. Should we expose a fallback cookie or an explicit SDK handshake call so apps can persist opt-in server-side?

marta: plan: SDK will expose initOptIn(userId, opts) which sets header on subsequent requests. For platforms that can't set headers reliably we will make a POST /client-optin endpoint the SDK can call so the control plane stores a short-lived opt-in token bound to the user id. server reads either header or token cookie.

aiden: Compliance flagged audit needs — any opt-in events must be logged with SDK version and originating app id. Also need revoke flow.

marta: noted. We'll emit an audit event: client_optin.created {user, sdk_version, app_id, rid}. Revoke via SDK call or server TTL.

li: Another gotcha: routing QoS. If canary endpoints saturate we need a guard that ignores client opt-in and falls back to default model. We should ensure telemetry surfaces how many requests came from client opt-ins.

marta: agreed — routing policy will accept header but still evaluate capacity and an opt-in guard flag. Telemetry plan: tag traces with client_optin=1 and shard=rid. Dashboards: client-optin traffic, error-rate, latency p50/p95 for opt-in vs default.

jasper: Implementation notes for SDKs:
- expose initOptIn and revokeOptIn
- header only present after initOptIn succeeds
- keep header under 64 bytes
- include x-redwood-trace for linking to traces

marta: small security note: opt_in token should be HMAC'd with SDK key so servers can validate and avoid spoofing. We'll add a short MAC suffix if feasible.

sre-bot: reminder: make sure request sampling includes opt-in traces at higher rate for early rollouts.

deploy-bot: Feature flag client-optin-header toggled: dev=on, staging=on, prod=off.

ben: +1. final ask: update console UX so product owners can opt to honor client opt-ins per rollout. Otherwise teams will be confused why header has no effect.

marta: will add a per-rollout toggle (Honor client opt-in) and docs for SDK behaviors. Thanks everyone, I'll put up the RFC and a short SDK spec.
